| [AM.MAN.METHOD.RL.1] <a id="am-man-method-rl-1"></a> | **SGS｜RL · Success-guided sampling · Training-reset scheduling**<br>[A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.12465v1)<br>Octi Zhang, Mateo Guaman Castro, Patrick Yin, Ignacio Dagnino, Abhishek Gupta, Rosario Scalise, Byron Boots<br>**Tags:** `manipulation` `gripper` [reinforcement-learning](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `success-guided-sampling` `adaptive-curriculum` `reset-distribution` `training-start-scheduling` `massively-parallel-simulation` `contact-rich-assembly` `quadruped-locomotion` `teacher-student-distillation` `dagger` `rgb-policy` `sim-to-real` | SGS uses recent success rates for task configurations to prioritize training resets that are neither mastered nor currently out of reach, directing more parallel PPO experience toward learnable configurations and improving large-scale robot RL efficiency and capabilities.<br>**Evaluation scope:** A Beta-shaped weight over recent success rates samples a fixed configuration pool, retaining nonzero probability for easy/hard cases. Configurations specify initial state, goal and environment; manipulation resets cover reaching, stable grasp and near-goal starts, with coverage supplied externally. SGS only schedules training; PPO learns actions. Simulation covers 13 quadruped terrain types, six UR5e + Robotiq 2F-85 assembly tasks and Franka parallel-gripper nut-and-bolt assembly. Locomotion uses one multi-terrain policy; manipulation trains per task. At one million environments, Franka nut-and-bolt success is about 70% versus 6% for uniform sampling; simpler tasks benefit less at sufficient scale. DAgger distills UR5e point-cloud teachers into dual-view RGB/proprioceptive students that issue closed-loop end-effector translation/rotation increments and gripper commands on hardware without real-data fine-tuning: nut-and-bolt 18/48, rod insertion 30/49, gear mesh 47/50. This is neither multi-finger-hand validation nor a shared cross-platform policy.
